Bidang. Skirt made from a rectangular panel of brown cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube. The cotton is woven with blue stripes of varying thicknesses.

Bidang. Cotton skirt decorated with woven curvilinear motifs. Bidang. Skirt of woven cotton decorated with woven curvilinear motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; blue band on short edges; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, brown, and white along top and bottom; curvilinear patterns in the middle in brown and cream.

Bidang. Tubular skirt with geometrical pattern in the colours of brown and light red brown. The upper part of the skirt has a thick brown horizontal border followed by 5 smaller bands in the colours of yellow, brown and red, separated by a horizontal boarder with vertical small lines in the colours of black and white. The same pattern is repeated for the lower part of the skirt. There are 53 white cotton pieces with numbers on them from 1 to 53, written in order in brown pen/marker.

Bidang. Cotton skirt decorated with woven geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, and blue; curvilinear patterns in light blue; entire panel has been dipped in indigo slightly altering the colours.

Bidang. Skirt of woven cotton decorated with woven geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of blue, red, yellow, and white along top and bottom; geometric patterns in brown and red on a grey background in the middle; grey colour created from overdying indigo with red. Marked with pattern identification numbers.

Bidang. Cotton skirt decorated with woven geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, blue, and white; curvilinear patterns in light brown and white on a brown background in the central panel.

Bidang or Kain Selam. Skirt or diving cloth of blue woven cotton decorated with woven geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, and white; curvilinear patterns in white on the central panel, possibly representing a swimming animal or human.

Skirt - Skirt ("bidang") made of embroidered cloth ("kain sunkit"). Red and black embroidered pattern threads turned back at border stripes. Latter are of red, yellow and black and enclose three narrow white stripes, which are embroidered in red and black. Very uneven spacing of warp threads; in pattern stripes, mostly paired with occasional single warps, and arranged similarly in border stripes. Weft comprises two white parallel threads, right across cloth between each pattern pick; eight parallel strands of red or four of black for pattern picks

Bidang. Skirt of cream cotton decorated with woven stripes and embroidered geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, blue, and white along top and bottom; curvilinear patterns consisting of swirling lines in cream brought out through embroidery of alternating stripes in black and red wool.

Bidang. Skirt of woven cotton decorated with ikat geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of woven cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; wide border of blue with white, red and yellow stripes along top and bottom; bands of geometric patterns in white, black and brown on a dark brown background and thin stripes of red, yellow and black; motifs include crossing the river, hand spinning wheel, spear with one barb and tangkong creeper. Numbered fabric labels identify individual motifs.

Kain maba. Brown tubular skirt decoarted with geometrical patterns and circular and curved lines. Top and bottom have 4 lines each in the colours of black,red, orange, light yellow and pink. The cloth is rectangular and has been swon together with white thread at one end. The skirt is presumebly inside out and there are 45 pieces of small white cotton sewn into with each side representing a number from 1 to 45. They are sewn in various places with 20 on one side and 25 on the other. The numbers are written in order and in brown pen/marker.

Bidang or Kain Pampul. Skirt of woven pink cotton decorated with woven curvilinear motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, white, and blue along top and bottom; curvilinear patterns consisting of swirling lines in cream and blue.

Bidang. Skirt of woven cotton decorated with woven geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, yellow, black, and white; curvilinear patterns in light brown and white on a brown background in the central panel; each side is slightly different, with one side having more diamond shapes.

Bidang. Skirt of woven cotton decorated with ikat geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of woven cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border of black and red along top and bottom; bands of geometric patterns in white and red on a black background and thin stripes of yellow, red, white and black.

Bidang. Skirt of woven red cotton decorated with woven curvilinear motifs. Rectangular panel of cotton with the two ends sewn together to form a tube; border formed of stripes of red, blue, and white along top and bottom; curvilinear patterns consisting of swirling lines in cream and blue; motifs include flowers and branches.

Kalambi. Woman's jacket made from reddish brown cotton. Open at the front; sleeves are sewn on to body and are open at the armpit. Applied panel on the upper part of the back; outlined with an inner strip of red wool and an outer strip of yellow wool; contains embroidered geometric designs in blue and red on a white background.
Very finely woven jacket with red warp and weft with embroidered patterns

Kalambi Burong. Jacket made from cotton woven with geometric designs. Open at the front with red wool border on front edges, neck opening, and bottom edge; three thin cords attached on one side, probably part of a closure; pattern of vertical bands of brown, yellow, and black stripes alternating with bands of geometric motifs in brown and black; sleeves are attached; armpit area is not sewn shut. Woven panel attached to the back at the bottom with border of attached zig-zag trim; pattern consists of diamond shapes in white, pink, black, and yellow.

Kalambi Burong. Jacket made from cotton woven with geometric designs. Open at the front with red wool border on front edges, neck opening, and bottom edge; one rectangular wool strip applied on each side on the front about halfway down; two pieces of cord attached to one side, possibly part of a closure; pattern of vertical bands of brown, yellow, and blue stripes alternating with bands of geometric motifs in brown and red; solid section of brown pattern on a red background on the front, back, and in the middle of the sleeves containing bird and frog motifs; sleeves are attached; armpit area is not sewn shut.

Kalambi Burong. Woman's jacket made from cotton woven with vertical stripes. Open at the front; pattern of vertical bands of pink, yellow, white, and brown stripes alternating with bands of geometric motifs, including lizards, in brown and reddish brown; section of solid brown about halfway down on the front; sleeves are sewn on to body. At the bottom on the back there is a horizontal panel of yellow, red, white, and blue in a diamond pattern; horizontal row of double twining in brown and white above this.

Kalambi Burong. Jacket made from cotton woven with geometric designs. Open at the front with red wool border on front edges, neck opening, cuffs, and bottom edge; large silver gilt button attached just below the neck opening on ones side; pattern of vertical bands of brown, red, white, and black stripes alternating with bands of geometric motifs in brown and tan; segment of brown across the jacket halfway down; sleeves are attached; armpit area is not sewn shut. Woven panel attached to the back at the bottom with border of red and yellow wool; pattern consists of wavy lines and blocks of colour in white, red, black, blue, brown, and yellow.

Kalambi Burong. Woman's sleeveless coat or tunic made of cotton and decorated with nassa shells. Indigo-dyed exterior lined with striped brown cotton interior; open at the front with three buttons attached on the proper right on the interior using thin cord. Nassa shells that have been filed down are attached using pineapple leaf fibre cord; shells attached in scroll design with triangles around the bottom; shells in the form of a monitor lizard on the back. The front edges, seams, and armholes are covered by a red cloth, which now appears brown.
Patterned loincloth with red cloth and glass bead fringe at the base and decorated with bronze hawk-bells.

Each band consists of alternating red and black embroidered triangles. The main embroidery consists of geometric patterns in red and black and chevrons of blue. Strip of orange and blue cloth attached at one end. Pattern identification numbers stitched onto one side.

Dangdong. Shawl of woven cotton decorated with geometric motifs. Rectangular panel of woven cotton with strip of black cloth applied on the back at each short end; border formed of stripes of red, brown, white, orange, and green; geometric patterns in cream and brown on a red background in the central panel consisting of swirling lines and diamond shapes.

Dangdong. Shawl, coverlet. Dull Indian red forms the background to the pale buff patterns, which have a touch of darker brown. At the side there are three patterned stripes, divided by composite ones, containing red, white, black and yellow pin stripes.

Kalambi Ara. Woman's jacket made from cotton woven with vertical stripes.
